subject: health
unitTitle: Safety, Injury Prevention, and Digital Life
title: Correction and reflection: recognising unsafe requests and refusing
essentialQuestion: How do I prevent harm and respond well when something goes wrong?
materials: a basic first-aid kit for inspection with an adult
a properly fitted helmet or protective gear if relevant
keyPoints: Warning signs: secrecy, flattery, gifts, urgency, isolating you, or asking you to break a family rule.
Online grooming often begins friendly and moves slowly towards secrets and images.
A refusal is short and repeated; you do not owe an explanation, and you may simply leave or log off.
Requests for photos of your body always get a no and always get reported to a trusted adult.
You will not be in trouble for telling, even if you already replied or already agreed.
privacySafeScenario: Someone met in a game says they are 11, sends a gift code, asks for a photo, and says not to tell. Identify every warning sign and give the full response.
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about recognising unsafe requests and refusing to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Name one thing you corrected or would do differently, and one other place recognising unsafe requests and refusing would be useful.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about recognising unsafe requests and refusing.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: First-aid content is taught as recognition and when-to-get-help, not as independent treatment. Any hands-on step may be observed, described, or demonstrated by the adult instead of performed by the learner.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about recognising unsafe requests and refusing under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, check that everyone in the household knows the home address and one emergency contact number by heart. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
